title: 你的搭讪为什么没卵用？什么是有效搭讪

timeline.summary: Cold-open field interaction: Mikey asks to meet a woman, exchanges brief personal/scheduling talk and appears to add WeChat; later outcome is not shown.
Studio explanation defines effective versus ineffective approaches and argues that collecting a contact alone does not show positive impression, skill growth or likelihood of meeting again.

Signal one is whether the person voluntarily stops. Mikey warns not to keep following someone who continues walking and says to let her leave; field examples illustrate both stopping and mistaking an approach for sales.
Signal two is eye contact. Mikey treats it as attention and a cue to the approacher's state, then a field example includes an explicit acknowledgment that prolonged staring can feel awkward.
Signal three is continued conversation after the opening, framed as an opportunity for mutual information and personality to become visible; a field clip shows occupational talk.

Signal four is not rejecting a romantic/sexual frame. Mikey contrasts it with purely polite or friendship interaction, disclaims explicit sexual harassment, and recommends skipping contact collection when the frame is not accepted.
Commercial call to contact the team, channel sign-off and branded outro.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He defines an effective approach as receiving attention while leaving a sufficiently positive impression that a second meeting remains possible; collecting a contact by itself does not meet that standard.
claims.conditions: This is Mikey's coaching definition, not an objective measure. A number exchange can be politeness or a safety exit, and only later voluntary engagement can clarify interest.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He argues that repeating contact-collection openings without learning conversation, rapport or feedback can leave practice stuck at the courage-to-initiate stage.
claims.conditions: Do not treat strangers as practice equipment; every interaction must remain low-pressure, lawful and easy to exit.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: A person voluntarily stopping is his first practical sign that attention is available; if she keeps walking or does not want to stop, he explicitly says not to follow and to let her leave.
claims.conditions: Stopping only permits ordinary conversation; it does not prove attraction, consent to contact exchange, proximity, touch or continued pursuit.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He presents sustained eye contact as a sign of attention or interest and as information about the approacher's confidence and intent.
claims.conditions: Eye contact is culturally and individually variable and is not proof of attraction or consent; discomfort, avoidance or explicit words take priority.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He treats continued voluntary conversation after the opening as an opportunity for each person to learn more and for a clearer impression to form.
claims.conditions: Conversation duration alone does not prove interest; politeness, uncertainty, safety management or situational constraints may also explain it.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He says an approach should communicate romantic intent rather than hiding in a purely platonic script, while rejecting explicit sexual propositions or harassing words as the way to do so.
claims.conditions: His language of male 'aggression' and nonverbal romantic framing is underspecified. Romantic intent should be expressed plainly and respectfully, with no pressure; lack of clear reciprocation means stop rather than escalate.

examples.summary: Several edited street interactions illustrate stopping, mistaken-sales reactions, eye contact, continued talk and departure, but the montage does not show a complete attempt denominator or later dates.
In one clip, a woman says she initially thought the approach was sales and had run from earlier approaches; this is her localized account, not a rule about women generally.

speaker_attribution.speaker: Mikey
speaker_attribution.basis: Self-identifies at S00001 and appears as the single host in studio; teaching blocks and his own field lines are attributed to him by edit context.

speaker_attribution.speaker: approached women
speaker_attribution.basis: Short field replies are participant speech; they support only the visible exchange and cannot authorize Mikey's broader interpretations.

speaker_attribution.speaker: editorial captions and montage
speaker_attribution.basis: Burned-in labels such as '信号四' organize the video but do not independently verify interest, consent or outcomes.

visual_findings: All 10 sampled frames were reviewed. Frames 000002-000004 and 000006-000008 show Mikey delivering a direct-to-camera sofa monologue; frames 000001, 000005 and 000009 show public approaches; frame 000010 is the channel outro.
Frame 000008 contains the on-screen label '信号四：女人不排斥和你进入男女框架', confirming the fourth-part edit structure but not its psychological inference.
Public participants' faces and surrounding bystanders are visible. The samples do not establish notice, filming consent, publication consent or later contact outcomes.
The montage alternates examples with claims; editing prevents treating every reaction as a continuous or representative interaction.

permissions.reason: Distinct source, but the four-signal model overreads attention cues as interest, uses gender-wide claims and ambiguous aggressive/sexual framing, and relies on edited public footage with unresolved privacy and consent.

limitations: Automatic transcript was not checked word-for-word against original audio.
Ten 45-second sampled frames do not equal continuous audio-visual review.
The edited examples do not provide the full number of attempts, voluntary contact validity, later replies, meetings or outcomes.
Stopping, eye contact and conversation duration are ambiguous social cues and cannot substitute for explicit consent or clear reciprocal interest.
Filming and publication consent for approached people and bystanders are unknown.
